stories.headline: Met Office weather update for Sutton Bridge
stories.brief: The Met Office has issued a weather update for the Sutton Bridge area in Lincolnshire. Residents are advised to check the latest forecasts for any potential changes to local conditions. Further information regarding the current outlook can be found via the official Met Office website.

stories.headline: New biogas plant proposed for Chatteris
stories.brief: Pretoria Energy has submitted a proposal to build a second biogas facility in Chatteris. The company intends to construct the new plant directly alongside its existing site in the town. Further details regarding the scale of the project or the timeline for development have not yet been released.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn students raise funds for Breast Cancer Now
stories.brief:
Hair and Beauty students at the College of West Anglia in King’s Lynn have raised over £135 for the charity Breast Cancer Now. During a recent ‘Wear It Pink’ event, students provided treatments including manicures and deep conditioning to members of the public. 

The fundraiser allowed students to gain professional experience while encouraging important conversations about breast cancer awareness and symptoms. Course director Holly Little praised the group for their enthusiasm in combining practical learning with charitable support. The event served as the first opportunity this academic year for many of the students to work directly with clients.

stories.headline: Peterborough United and Norwich City draw in women's football
stories.brief: Peterborough United and Norwich City played out a draw in their recent women's football fixture. The match between the two clubs ended with a final score of one-one.

stories.headline: Cambridgeshire locations named among best places to live
stories.brief: Eight areas across Cambridgeshire have been highlighted as the best places to live in the county. The list, published by Cambridge News, identifies these locations as stunning areas within the region. No further details regarding the specific towns or villages included in the selection were provided in the report.

stories.headline: Red Arrows to fly over Cambridgeshire this week
stories.brief: Residents across Cambridgeshire are being advised that the Red Arrows are scheduled to fly over the county this week. The display team is expected to be visible in the skies as part of their current flight schedule. Those hoping to catch a glimpse of the aircraft are encouraged to look out for them throughout the coming days. Further details regarding specific timings and locations have been reported by The Hunts Post.

stories.headline: College of West Anglia hosts sixth annual Operation Inspire careers event
stories.brief:
Students at the College of West Anglia’s King’s Lynn campus have taken part in the sixth annual Operation Inspire event. Held during T Levels week at the college’s sports campus, the careers fair connected students with a wide range of employers, universities, and training providers.

Organisations from sectors including healthcare, the Armed Forces, public services, and fitness were in attendance to offer career guidance and work experience information. The event, which was opened by West Norfolk Mayor Cllr Steve Bearshaw, aims to help students explore future employment pathways and build professional networks. Staff from HMP Whitemoor at March were among those represented, providing interactive demonstrations for the students in attendance.

stories.headline: New road repair trials begin on Cambridgeshire peat land
stories.brief: Cambridgeshire County Council has launched a series of trials to test new ways of maintaining roads built on peat. Seven different repair methods are being used in a project described as a first for the UK. The initiative aims to find more effective solutions for the specific challenges posed by the region's unique ground conditions. Officials hope these tests will lead to more durable road surfaces across the area.

stories.headline: Funding secured for new £600,000 fire training centre in King’s Lynn
stories.brief:
A new £600,000 specialist training facility is planned for the South Lynn fire station. The project is being funded by a joint investment of £300,000 each from Norfolk County Council and West Norfolk Council. The site will allow crews to practice for complex emergencies, including road traffic collisions and rescues at height, without needing to travel to other stations. 

Construction is expected to begin next year, subject to planning consent and site surveys. Officials say the facility will help firefighters maintain vital skills locally and ensure emergency services can keep pace with the area's growing population. The development follows a record-breaking summer for Norfolk Fire and Rescue Service, which saw its busiest month on record this August.

stories.headline: Peterborough United Women to face Norwich City
stories.brief: Peterborough United Women are set to play Norwich City in an upcoming football fixture. The match between the two clubs has been confirmed, with details regarding the preview released by Norwich City Football Club. Supporters are advised to check official club channels for further information regarding the game.

stories.headline: Autumn walking spots highlighted in Cambridgeshire
stories.brief: A new report from The Hunts Post has identified five locations across Cambridgeshire recommended for autumn walks. The publication highlights these areas as suitable destinations for residents looking to enjoy the seasonal scenery. While specific locations were not detailed in the report, the information serves as a guide for those planning outdoor activities in the county during the coming weeks.

stories.headline: New 'Perch Here' trail opens in Sutton Bridge
stories.brief: A new walking route called the 'Perch Here' trail has officially launched in Sutton Bridge. The project was introduced by Lincolnshire County Council. Residents and visitors are now able to access the trail, which is designed to encourage walking in the local area. Further details regarding the route and its features are available through the council’s official channels.

stories.headline: Police investigate suspected car fire in Fenland town
stories.brief: Cambridgeshire police are investigating a suspected arson attack following a vehicle fire in a Fenland town. Officers are currently looking into the circumstances surrounding the incident. No further details regarding the exact location or the condition of the vehicle have been released at this time. Anyone with information is encouraged to contact the authorities.

stories.headline: Vehicle seized by police on the A47 in Wisbech
stories.brief:
Police in Fenland have seized a van following a stop on the A47 near the Elm Hall roundabout in Wisbech. Officers from the local neighbourhood team pulled the vehicle over after noticing it was being driven with an exploded tyre.

Upon inspection, the driver was reported for several offences, including driving without a valid licence or insurance. They were also reported for operating a vehicle with an insecure load. The van has since been removed from the road.

stories.headline: Repairs approved for historic King’s Lynn South Gate
stories.brief:
West Norfolk Council has granted listed building consent for maintenance work at the historic South Gate in King’s Lynn. The project includes replacing a window on the western side, installing a new internal timber screen, and repointing brickwork around the main gateway on London Road. 

Architects state the repairs are necessary to prevent further degradation of the masonry and to keep the site secure. While the council has approved the plans, there is currently no confirmed start date for the work. It remains unclear if the repairs will require any traffic restrictions on London Road or what the total cost of the project will be. Historic England has expressed support for the proposed maintenance.

stories.headline: Roof repairs scheduled for Long Sutton Library
stories.brief: Lincolnshire County Council has announced that essential roof replacement work is set to take place at Long Sutton Library. The local authority confirmed the project is necessary to maintain the building. Residents are advised to check for any potential service updates or temporary changes to library access while these improvements are carried out.

stories.headline: Rescue team saves deer from farm pool
stories.brief: A small deer has been rescued after becoming trapped in a pool on a local farm. A specialist rescue team was called to the scene to assist the animal. No further details regarding the location of the farm or the condition of the deer have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Gaywood fundraiser completes six-week wheelchair challenge
stories.brief:
A Gaywood man has raised approximately £2,500 for the limbless veterans charity, Blesma, after completing six half marathons in six consecutive weeks. 56-year-old Mark Howard, who has used a wheelchair since 2015, travelled across the country to take part in the events between September 13 and October 18. 

Mr Howard, a former soldier, described the feat as his toughest challenge to date due to the lack of recovery time between races. Despite medical advice to reduce his activity due to shoulder strain, he is now planning to launch a club next Easter to provide others with access to specialist equipment like wheelchairs and handcycles. Local residents interested in his upcoming projects can contact him on 07780463643.

stories.headline: Peterborough knocked out of Carabao Cup
stories.brief: Peterborough United have been eliminated from the Carabao Cup following a defeat against Bradford City. The match concluded with a two-nil victory for the home side.

stories.headline: Nine Cambridgeshire council staff dismissed following disciplinary action
stories.brief: Figures reported by the Ely East Cambridgeshire News reveal that nine council employees in Cambridgeshire were dismissed over the past year. These departures followed a series of formal disciplinary hearings conducted by the local authority. No further details regarding the specific departments involved or the nature of the misconduct have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Spalding man cultivates Italian-style olive grove
stories.brief: A resident of the Spalding area is successfully growing olives using traditional Italian methods. The project, which has been highlighted by the BBC, sees the local grower adapting Mediterranean cultivation techniques for the Fenland climate. The story of the so-called "Crazy Englishman" and his unusual agricultural venture has drawn attention for its unique approach to farming in South Holland.

stories.headline: Cambridgeshire Wetherspoons pubs highlighted in new report
stories.brief: A recent report from Peterborough Matters has identified seven Wetherspoons pubs across Cambridgeshire as top-rated venues for visitors. The publication highlights these specific locations as recommended spots for those looking to dine or drink in the county. While the list focuses on sites within the wider Cambridgeshire area, residents are encouraged to check the full details online if they are planning a visit to any of these establishments.

stories.headline: Double musical success for King’s Lynn school
stories.brief:
Springwood High School in King’s Lynn is celebrating a double achievement in music education. The school has been reappointed as the Lead School for West Norfolk by the Norfolk and Suffolk Music Hub for a second consecutive year. Additionally, the school has received a nomination for the Music Mark of Recognition for Ambition and Quality in Music Education.

Director of music Robin Norman says the school is bucking national trends, with student participation in instrumental and singing lessons reaching 12.5 per cent. Furthermore, enrollment for GCSE and A-Level music courses has doubled since the pandemic. The school continues to support music provision across the local area as part of its lead role.

stories.headline: Recent cases heard at King’s Lynn Magistrates’ Court
stories.brief:
King’s Lynn Magistrates’ Court dealt with a series of cases last week involving theft, driving offences, and arson. Among those appearing were several prolific shoplifters, including James Leonard, who reached his 200th recorded offence after stealing items from a local store. Other defendants faced sentencing for supermarket thefts in Downham, Sheringham, and Fakenham.

The court also addressed driving offences, including individuals caught without valid licences or insurance, and a case of arson at the St James Multi-Storey Car Park. Additionally, magistrates heard cases involving public order offences, drug possession, and the assault of a police officer. Defendants received various penalties, ranging from fines and community orders to custodial sentences.

stories.headline: Police investigate stabbing outside Littleport Co-op
stories.brief: Two men have been stabbed in an incident outside the Co-op store in Littleport. Reports describe the attack as unprovoked. Local authorities are currently investigating the circumstances surrounding the event. Anyone with information regarding the incident is encouraged to contact the police.

stories.headline: Roadworks scheduled for A17 between Holbeach and Sutton Bridge
stories.brief: Drivers in the Fens should prepare for disruption this weekend as surfacing works begin on the A17. Lincolnshire County Council has confirmed that the maintenance project will take place on the stretch of road located between Holbeach and Sutton Bridge. Motorists are advised to plan their journeys accordingly while these improvements are carried out.

stories.headline: Eight-week road closure near Chatteris
stories.brief: Drivers in the Fens should prepare for disruption near Chatteris. A road in the area is set to be closed for eight weeks to allow for essential repair work to take place. Motorists are advised to plan their journeys accordingly while these works are carried out.

stories.headline: Rock Choir raises over £1,000 for Army Benevolent Fund
stories.brief:
Members of the King’s Lynn and Peterborough Rock Choir have raised more than £1,100 for the Army Benevolent Fund. The group performed at Downham Market’s Methodist Church on Saturday, October 3, as part of the church’s 60th birthday celebrations. 

The concert featured two 50-minute sets of popular hits, with funds collected through ticket sales and refreshments. The Army Benevolent Fund provides ongoing support to soldiers, veterans, and their families. Choir leader Sally Rose thanked the audience for their participation and support during the event. Those interested in joining the Rock Choir can find more information on their official website.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn Town Hall to host memorial lecture on Margery Kempe
stories.brief:
King’s Lynn Town Hall will host the 12th annual Pat Midgley Memorial Lecture on Thursday, November 19. Organised by True’s Yard Fisherfolk Museum, the event runs from 7pm to 8pm in the Stone Hall and will be hosted by the Mayor of West Norfolk, Councillor Steve Bearshaw.

Speakers Mirabelle Dominé-Walley and Luke Walker will present a lecture and film titled "Margery Kempe and the Wash." The presentation examines the life of the medieval mystic alongside traditional fishing practices on the Wash. Tickets are priced at £5 and include refreshments. The lecture honours the late Pat Midgley, who founded the museum and helped preserve historic fisherfolk cottages in the town.

stories.headline: Peterborough United match postponed
stories.brief: The upcoming football match between Peterborough United and Oxford United has been called off. The fixture was postponed due to international call-ups affecting the squads. Supporters are advised that the game will no longer take place as originally scheduled.

stories.headline: Five Cambridgeshire locations suggested for autumn walks
stories.brief: Residents looking to enjoy the changing season have been offered a list of five recommended spots for autumn walks across Cambridgeshire. The suggestions were published by the Wisbech Standard, highlighting various locations suitable for outdoor activity as the weather turns. Those interested in exploring the local countryside can find the full list of recommended sites on the Ely East Cambridgeshire News website.

stories.headline: Positive coronavirus tests confirmed at Lincolnshire school
stories.brief: A school in Lincolnshire has reported a number of positive coronavirus cases. The institution confirmed that several individuals have tested positive for the virus. No further details regarding the specific location of the school or the number of people affected have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Potholes reported on road near Wisbech before fatal collision
stories.brief: Images have emerged showing potholes on a road in the vicinity of Wisbech. According to reports from the BBC, these photographs were taken just days before a fatal crash occurred at the location. No further details regarding the incident or the specific road involved have been released at this time.

stories.headline: A10 roadwork delays in West Winch
stories.brief:
Overnight roadworks on the A10 near West Winch have been extended until Saturday, October 31. The project, which involves survey work for the new West Winch Housing Access Road, was delayed due to difficulties accessing local drains. Lane closures and temporary traffic lights remain in place between 8pm and 6am on a section of the A10 near the Gravel Hill Lane junction. 

Meanwhile, planned surveys on the A47 and Hardwick Roundabout are still scheduled to begin on Monday, October 26. Norfolk County Council has apologised for the disruption and expects all survey work to conclude by the end of November. Noisy activities are restricted to before 11pm each night.

stories.headline: New book examines the impact of the 1643 Siege of King’s Lynn
stories.brief:
A new book by local historian James Rye explores the long-term consequences of the 1643 Civil War siege of King’s Lynn. Titled "The Siege of King’s Lynn 1643: A Port Divided and the Cost of Civil War," the work details how the three-week conflict affected trade, property repairs, and the lives of local residents. 

Mr Rye utilised contemporary records and archaeological research to document the challenges faced by the town following its negotiated surrender. The book features historical figures including Thomas Toll and Alice L’Estrange. It is currently available for purchase online, priced at £7.99 for the paperback edition or £4.99 for the eBook.

stories.headline: Peterborough United manager expresses confidence in squad
stories.brief: Peterborough United manager Robbie Savage has stated that his team is capable of defeating any opponent. The comments follow the club's recent performances as they look ahead to upcoming fixtures. Savage remains optimistic about the squad's potential for the remainder of the season.

stories.headline: MP calls for £500 million investment to fix Cambridgeshire roads
stories.brief: A local Member of Parliament is campaigning for half a billion pounds in funding to address the condition of roads across Cambridgeshire. The proposed investment is intended to repair routes built on weak soil, which have been identified as a significant issue for the county's infrastructure. The bid for £500 million aims to tackle the ongoing maintenance challenges caused by the region's specific ground conditions.

stories.headline: Dispersal orders issued for Holbeach and Sutton Bridge
stories.brief: Lincolnshire Police have put two 48-hour dispersal orders in place for Holbeach and Sutton Bridge. These orders grant officers additional powers to move individuals out of the designated areas for a set period. Residents in these parts of the Fens should be aware that the measures are now active. Police have not provided further details regarding the specific reasons for the orders or the exact boundaries of the affected zones.

stories.headline: Update announced for Whittlesey leisure centre project
stories.brief: Plans for a new leisure centre in Whittlesey have reached a significant milestone. The proposed facility, which carries an estimated cost of 18.7 million pounds, is the subject of a major update. Further details regarding the development are expected as the project progresses.

stories.headline: Wisbech Christmas fair returns this December
stories.brief:
The annual Wisbech Christmas fair is set to return to the town centre on Sunday, December 13. Running from 10am until 3pm, the free event will feature live music, including a brass band, alongside various stalls and food vendors. Families can enjoy activities at the library, miniature train rides on Market Street, and visits with Santa. 

Visitors are encouraged to walk, cycle, or use public transport, as road closures and parking restrictions will be in effect. Free parking will be available at several council car parks and the Horsefair Shopping Centre. Additionally, the March Christmas Market is scheduled for the previous Sunday, December 6, also running from 10am to 3pm.

stories.headline: Downham Market toddler stars in national swimming campaign
stories.brief:
A three-year-old from Downham Market is helping to front a new national initiative from Swim England. Phoebe Stoves and her grandmother, Gill, are featured in the ‘Love Swimming’ campaign, which highlights the benefits of pool sessions for families. 

Phoebe began lessons in April and has since grown in confidence after initially feeling nervous. The campaign, supported by Alive West Norfolk, encourages families to start swimming lessons this autumn. Research suggests that most children show improved water confidence after only a few sessions. Those interested in finding local classes can visit the Swim England website at swimming.org/poolfinder for more information.

stories.headline: Nearly 90 dogs seized from Spalding property
stories.brief: Authorities have seized almost 90 dogs from a property in Spalding. The operation took place over the weekend. No further details regarding the circumstances of the seizure or the current welfare of the animals have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Hunstanton man reaches 200th conviction for shoplifting
stories.brief:
A 59-year-old man from Hunstanton has appeared in court after reaching a milestone of 200 criminal convictions. James Leonard, of Park Road, pleaded guilty at Lynn Magistrates’ Court on Thursday to stealing two Mars bars and a fizzy drink from the One Beyond store in King’s Lynn. The items, valued at £4.69, were taken on September 12.

During the hearing, the court heard that Leonard expressed disappointment in his own actions. Magistrates fined him £45 and ordered him to pay a £16 victim surcharge along with £45 in court costs.

stories.headline: Peterborough council considers new firework restrictions
stories.brief: Peterborough City Council is considering a new Public Space Protection Order aimed at reducing firework-related nuisance in the area. The proposed measures are designed to address concerns regarding the impact of fireworks on local residents. Further details on the scope of the order and how it might be enforced are expected to be discussed as the plans progress. Residents are advised to monitor official council communications for updates on the potential implementation of these new rules.

stories.headline: Archaeological discovery in Littleport sheds light on Roman history
stories.brief: An archaeological excavation in Littleport has provided new insights into an early Roman field system. The findings have helped experts resolve long-standing questions regarding the layout and function of the site. Researchers believe the discovery offers a clearer understanding of how the land was managed during the Roman period in the region.

stories.headline: Queen Elizabeth Hospital receives £3.9m for winter urgent care
stories.brief:
The Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn has been awarded £3.9 million in government funding to boost urgent and emergency care services. The investment aims to help the hospital manage increased demand during the winter months by allowing staff to treat minor illnesses and injuries separately from emergency cases. 

Work to reconfigure the emergency department is already underway, with plans for a new urgent treatment centre to follow. Local MPs Terry Jermy and James Wild have welcomed the funding, though both continue to press for long-term commitments regarding the future of the hospital’s 24/7 A&E department. This grant is part of a wider £140 million national investment across 14 urgent care schemes in England.

stories.headline: Police arrest following break-in at services
stories.brief: Police have made an arrest in connection with a break-in at a service station. Officers are currently investigating the incident. No further details regarding the location or the identity of the individual arrested have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Proposed gate for Peterborough alleyway
stories.brief: A new gate has been proposed for an alleyway in Peterborough. The measure follows reports that the area is currently being used by drug users. The proposal aims to restrict access to the site.

stories.headline: Five recommended autumn walking spots in Cambridgeshire
stories.brief:
Residents looking to enjoy the changing season are being pointed towards five specific locations across Cambridgeshire for autumn walks. According to the Ely Standard, these sites have been highlighted as ideal spots to experience the local landscape during the coming months. 

Whether you are planning a weekend stroll or a shorter outing, these five areas offer opportunities to take in the autumn scenery across the county. Further details on the suggested routes and locations can be found in the latest report from the Ely Standard.

stories.headline: Concerns grow over potential maternity service changes in Norfolk
stories.brief:
Campaigners and MPs have raised concerns over the future of maternity services at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn and the James Paget Hospital in Gorleston. Both sites are among the smallest consultant-led units in England, and hospital bosses are currently reviewing healthcare strategies due to factors including falling birth rates.

While the Norfolk and Waveney University Hospitals Group insists no decisions have been made, there are fears that downgrading these units could force women to travel longer distances for care. Local leaders have argued that services should remain accessible and locally based. The clinical strategy is expected to be presented to the Norfolk County Council’s health overview and scrutiny committee next month.

stories.headline: Stem cell donor event held in King’s Lynn for baby Reuben
stories.brief:
The East of England Ambulance Service is hosting a stem cell swabbing event today at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn. The drive aims to find a life-saving donor for Reuben, a baby boy from Norfolk who was diagnosed with acute myeloid leukaemia at ten months old. 

Staff are welcoming potential donors at the ambulance station on Gayton Road until 6pm this evening. Those aged between 16 and 55 are encouraged to attend for a simple cheek swab to join the DKMS and Anthony Nolan registers. Anyone unable to visit the hospital site can also register online to request a home testing kit. Every new registration increases the chances of finding a match for Reuben and other patients worldwide.

stories.headline: New DC horror film Clay Face arrives at The Light in Wisbech
stories.brief: A new addition to the DC Universe is now showing at The Light cinema in Wisbech. The film, titled Clay Face, is an R-rated origin story focusing on the iconic Batman villain. It stars Tom Rhys Harries as Matt Hagen, an actor who undergoes an experimental nanite treatment after a brutal attack. The cast also features Naomi Ackie, Max Minghella, and Rob Brydon. While the film explores themes of vengeance and body horror, it has received praise for its performances and emotional depth. Local cinema-goers can catch the movie at the Wisbech venue now.

stories.headline: New management team takes over King’s Lynn hair and beauty salon
stories.brief:
A new team is now in charge at the House of Hair and Beauty on Tower Street in King’s Lynn. Manager Cole Ellis, who has over two decades of industry experience, is working alongside stylist Karyn Hardy to offer a range of hair treatments. The salon is currently looking to recruit additional stylists to fill available chairs and a beauty room. 

The business is located next to the Majestic Cinema and is open Tuesday to Saturday, from 9am until 5pm, with flexible late appointments available. New clients are currently being offered a 30 percent discount on treatments. Mr Ellis says he aims to create a welcoming, family-like atmosphere for both staff and customers.

stories.headline: Peterborough City Council announces new framework for 2027 to 2031
stories.brief: Peterborough City Council has unveiled a new framework covering the period from 2027 to 2031. Details regarding the upcoming project were reported by The Architects’ Journal. No further information has been released at this time regarding the specific nature or scope of the council's plans for this four-year window.

stories.headline: Concerns raised over illegal parking in Wisbech Market Place
stories.brief:
A resident has raised concerns regarding illegal parking in Wisbech Market Place, describing the area as an "open-air exhibition of parking delinquency." Photographs taken on the morning of October 23, 2026, show multiple vehicles parked in restricted areas, none of which displayed a blue badge. 

The resident also reported finding the Wisbech police station doors locked when attempting to report the issue in person, noting that visitors are instead directed to use an external telephone. Questions have been raised regarding current enforcement levels in the town compared to other parts of Fenland, as well as the process for reporting such contraventions when the local station is closed to the public.

stories.headline: Hundreds of West Norfolk pupils receive free dictionaries
stories.brief:
Hundreds of primary school children across King’s Lynn and West Norfolk have received free copies of the Usborne Illustrated Dictionary. The initiative, run by the three local Rotary clubs, has been operating for over a decade. This year, 950 books were distributed to pupils in Years 4 and 5 to support literacy and classroom learning.

Teachers report that the dictionaries are being used to help students with spelling, vocabulary, and creative writing. The books are provided at no cost to the children, with schools contributing one pound per copy and the Rotary clubs covering the remaining expense. The clubs involved include Trinity, Lynn, and Priory Rotary.

stories.headline: Calls for action over flooded Peterborough footpath
stories.brief: There are calls for new measures to address a flooded footpath in Peterborough. The route is reportedly causing issues for local school children, who are being left wet and muddy while trying to reach their classes. Concerns have been raised regarding the state of the path, prompting requests for authorities to take action to resolve the ongoing problem.

stories.headline: Ely restaurant could be converted into residential home
stories.brief: A restaurant in the Ely area may be transformed into a private residence. Planning documents indicate the business is currently facing significant operational pressures. The proposal to change the site's use from a commercial eatery to a home is now under consideration.

stories.headline: Obituary published for Norman Parnell
stories.brief: An obituary has been published for Norman Parnell, a resident of the Fenland area in Lincolnshire. The notice, which appeared in the Fenland Citizen, commemorates his life and passing in 2026. Further details regarding his life and funeral arrangements can be found through the Legacy obituary service.

stories.headline: Family pays tribute following fatal collision
stories.brief: The family of a teenager who died in a road collision have released a formal tribute. Cambridgeshire Constabulary confirmed the news, though no further details regarding the location or circumstances of the incident have been provided at this time.

stories.headline: Ely MP calls for emergency heating oil price cap
stories.brief: An estimated 12,500 households in Ely are facing rising costs for heating oil. In response to the financial pressure on residents, the local Member of Parliament has called for the introduction of an emergency price cap. The proposal aims to provide support for those relying on oil to heat their homes as prices remain a concern for the community.

stories.headline: Concerns raised over school toilet access in Lincolnshire
stories.brief: A parent has criticised toilet access policies at a local school. The individual, who has experience of the prison system, claimed that pupils face more restrictions when trying to use school facilities than inmates do while incarcerated. The comments were reported by LincsOnline.

stories.headline: Whittlesey property closed following anti-social behaviour
stories.brief: A residential property in Whittlesey has been shut down by authorities. Cambridgeshire Constabulary confirmed the action was taken in response to ongoing anti-social behaviour at the address. The closure order is now in effect for the location.

stories.headline: Olive production begins at Long Sutton farm
stories.brief: A farm in Long Sutton is now producing olives, citing changes in the local climate as a key factor. The Lincolnshire-based site has successfully adapted to the shifting weather patterns to cultivate the crop. This development marks a notable change in agricultural output for the area, as traditional farming practices in the Fens continue to evolve alongside the changing environment.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn running group hosts event to help women feel safe after dark
stories.brief:
A King’s Lynn running group is launching a new initiative to help women feel more confident exercising during the winter months. The Lynnsport Ladybirds are hosting a ‘Let’s Lift The Curfew’ session on Wednesday, October 28, between 6:15pm and 7:30pm. The event encourages women to walk, jog, or run in a group setting. 

Organisers say the initiative is part of the national ‘This Girl Can’ campaign, which highlights how safety concerns often limit women’s outdoor activities after dark. Coach Fabia Pollard says the session is open to everyone and aims to provide a supportive environment for those who may feel hesitant about exercising in the evening. Spaces for the event are free to book.

stories.headline: Peterborough United fans react to Robbie Savage’s arrival
stories.brief: Supporters of Peterborough United have been sharing their views on the recent appointment of Robbie Savage. According to reports from the Peterborough Telegraph, fan opinion on the new manager is mixed. Some supporters have expressed scepticism about the long-term future of the appointment, with some suggesting he may depart before the end of the season. Speculation among the fanbase includes the possibility of an exit by mutual consent or a move to a Championship-level club.

stories.headline: New housing development finished in Long Sutton
stories.brief: A total of 45 new homes have been completed in Long Sutton. The project was delivered by the housing provider Accent. The development is now finished, according to reports from Housing Digital.

stories.headline: Council error halts plans for new March school crossing
stories.brief: Plans for a new pedestrian crossing near schools in March have been cancelled following a council error. According to reports, the project will not proceed as originally intended due to a mistake made by the local authority. The crossing was intended to improve safety for pupils in the area, but the administrative oversight has now dashed hopes for its installation. No further details regarding the nature of the error or potential future alternatives have been provided at this time.

stories.headline: Watlington man fined for drug possession at King’s Lynn police centre
stories.brief:
A 31-year-old man from Watlington has been fined after being found in possession of cocaine while in police custody. Dominic Loasby, of Britton Close, appeared at King’s Lynn Magistrates’ Court on Thursday. The court heard that a bag containing the Class A drug fell from his trousers while he was at the town’s Police Investigation Centre. 

Loasby admitted to the offence, telling the court the drugs were for personal use and had been purchased for £10. His defence solicitor noted that he had been fully compliant with officers throughout the process. Magistrates ordered Loasby to pay an £80 fine, alongside a £32 victim surcharge and £50 in court costs.

stories.headline: New visitor and gift shop planned for March geese
stories.brief: A new visitor and gift shop is set to open in March, dedicated to the town’s geese. The project aims to provide a dedicated space for those interested in the local wildlife. Further details regarding the opening date or the specific location of the new facility have not yet been announced.

stories.headline: Historical look at coal deliveries in the Fens
stories.brief:
A historical drawing featured in the Lynn Museum’s latest column highlights how coal reached our region before the expansion of the railways. The artwork depicts the vessel Endeavour of Lynn unloading cargo on the shingle shores near Weybourne in 1849. 

During this mid-Victorian period, beach-landing coasters would ride the tide onto the coast to supply rural communities, households, and kilns. Because formal docks were unavailable, local labourers manually shovelled coal from the ship’s hold into carts or baskets directly on the beach. This method of transport was essential for distributing coal from the Midlands and the Northeast throughout the area before local rail networks were developed.

stories.headline: Union warns of potential food shortages following Princes factory strike
stories.brief: The Unite union has warned that industrial action at the Princes factory could result in food shortages. The strike, which involves staff at the site, has prompted concerns regarding the potential impact on supply chains. While the union has highlighted the risk to food availability, no further details regarding the duration of the walkout or specific product lines affected have been confirmed at this time. Residents across the Fens are advised to monitor the situation for any updates regarding local grocery supplies.

stories.headline: Residents report sewage smell in Cambridgeshire market town
stories.brief: People living in a Cambridgeshire market town are reporting a persistent and unpleasant odour. According to recent reports, the area is currently being affected by what has been described as a foul stench of sewage. No further details regarding the source of the smell or any potential action being taken have been provided at this time.

stories.headline: College of West Anglia students prepare for national skills finals
stories.brief:
Students from across the Fens have been recognised for reaching the national finals of the WorldSkills UK competition. A special event was held at the College of West Anglia to celebrate learners who successfully progressed through regional heats. 

Among those honoured were Keegan Hanks and Selene Coote from King’s Lynn, and Rianna Moore from Terrington St John. Other local finalists include Wisbech students Erika Rimkus, Finn Mcauley, and Paige Marshall, alongside Marc Watson from March. The national finals take place this November, where competitors will vie for bronze, silver, and gold medals in their respective vocational fields. College principal David Pomfret praised the students for reaching the top five per cent of entrants nationwide.

stories.headline: Peterborough United draw away at Bromley
stories.brief: Peterborough United finished their latest League One fixture with a share of the points. The match against Bromley ended in a one-all draw. Highlights of the game are available via Sky Sports.

stories.brief: Plans have been put forward that could see Soham Football Club transformed into a new training centre for adult education. The proposal, reported by the Ely East Cambridgeshire News, suggests the football club grounds as a potential location for the facility. No further details regarding the timeline or the scope of the training programmes have been confirmed at this stage. Residents are advised to keep an eye on local planning updates for further information regarding the future of the site.

stories.headline: Long Sutton woman enters not guilty plea to drink-drive charge
stories.brief: A woman from Long Sutton has appeared in court to deny a charge of being in charge of a motor vehicle while over the legal alcohol limit. The alleged incident took place in Fleet Hargate. The case is being reported by the Spalding South Holland News.

stories.headline: Remembering life-saving training at Gaywood Primary
stories.brief:
We are looking back at a first aid pilot scheme held for pupils at Gaywood Primary School in October 2013. The training was delivered by the team behind the SOS Project Safe Haven, which provided support in King's Lynn town centre. During the sessions, Year Six students were taught essential techniques, including how to perform CPR, apply bandages, and place someone in the recovery position. 

Headteacher Paul Shanks described the initiative as a fantastic experience for the children. He noted that the skills learned at that age are likely to be remembered, providing the students with the ability to assist others should an emergency situation ever arise.

stories.headline: Man jailed for long-term abuse
stories.brief: A man has been sentenced to time in prison following a lengthy period of abuse. Cambridgeshire Constabulary confirmed the conviction, which follows an investigation into offences committed over several years. No further details regarding the location or the specific nature of the case have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Looking back at local history in King’s Lynn and Downham Market
stories.brief:
This week’s look back at local archives highlights two notable moments from the past. In 1961, King’s Lynn Town Council discussed ambitious plans to pedestrianise the High Street and considered the compulsory purchase of the Reffley Estate for new housing. Meanwhile, a new factory for Unicam Instruments was proposed for the Hardwick Road trading estate, with the potential to create 450 jobs.

Moving to 1994, Downham Market Town Hall hosted a special "Who Can Tell?" fun day. The event featured storytellers, musicians, and entertainers, forming part of a two-month festival across West and North Norfolk designed to encourage children to enjoy reading.

stories.headline: Peterborough United secure point against Bromley
stories.brief: Peterborough United earned a draw in their latest away fixture against Bromley. The result was secured after a goal from substitute Masara, who opened his account for the club during the match. The point is considered a valuable addition for the team as they continue their campaign.

stories.headline: Cambridge man defends world tiddlywinks title
stories.brief: A Cambridge resident has successfully defended his world title at the latest tiddlywinks championship. The competitor managed to retain his crown at the event, maintaining his status as the reigning world champion.

stories.headline: Students protest toilet policy at University Academy Long Sutton
stories.brief: Pupils at University Academy Long Sutton have staged a protest regarding changes to the school's toilet regulations. The demonstration follows the introduction of new rules concerning student access to facilities at the site. Further details regarding the specific nature of the policy changes or the school's response have not been released at this time.

stories.headline: New arrival for Chatteris fire crew
stories.brief: Cambridgeshire Fire and Rescue Service has announced a new addition to the team based in Chatteris. The service confirmed that firefighters at the station have been joined by a new colleague. No further details regarding the nature of the appointment have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Former Wisbech Town FC president returns to watch match
stories.brief:
A resident of Orchard House Care Home in Wisbech has enjoyed a special return to his former football club. John Petch, who served as president of Wisbech Town Football Club for 16 years, expressed a wish to see his hometown team play once again. Staff from the care home arranged for Mr Petch and his wife, Sheila, to attend Saturday’s match, which included lunch at Bygones. 

Mr Petch, who stepped down from his role in 2020 after nearly 60 years of service, was greeted by many familiar faces, including club chairman Paul Brenchley. He described the experience as a fantastic day, made even better by a victory for the home side.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn Waterstones highlights new book on paranormal investigations
stories.brief: Waterstones in King’s Lynn has named Chasing the Dark by Ben Machell as its current Book of the Week. The non-fiction title explores the history of the Society for Psychical Research, focusing on the work of British naval officer Tony Cornell. Between 1950 and 2010, Cornell was a prolific investigator of psychic phenomena and paranormal events, working alongside psychologist Alan Gauld to document reports from the public. The book draws on a previously untapped archive of Cornell’s case files, examining encounters with ghosts and poltergeists. The publication is currently featured alongside the store's latest top ten bestsellers list.

stories.headline: Developer appeals butterfly park planning decision
stories.brief: A developer is challenging a decision to refuse planning permission for a proposed butterfly park. The move has prompted concerns from local residents. The project, which was previously rejected by planning authorities, is now the subject of an appeal process. Further details regarding the timeline for the appeal or the specific reasons for the initial refusal have not been disclosed.

stories.headline: Cambridgeshire Wetherspoons pubs highlighted in recent report
stories.brief: A recent report from the Wisbech Standard has identified seven Wetherspoons pubs across Cambridgeshire as top-rated venues for visitors. The publication highlights these locations as recommended spots for those looking to dine or drink within the county. Residents and visitors interested in the full list of these highly-rated establishments can find further details on the Wisbech Standard website.

stories.headline: Rail operator pledges improvements to Fen Line services
stories.brief:
Great Northern has acknowledged that recent performance on the King’s Lynn Fen Line has been challenging for passengers. The operator says it is working to rebuild customer confidence following a rise in cancellations during September. North West Norfolk MP James Wild has been meeting with rail executives to press for better reliability, citing the impact of disruptions on commuters.

The operator reports that cancellations on the route fell by two-thirds between late September and mid-October. Efforts are now underway to improve fleet reliability and staff availability. The company is also working to restore a normal timetable between Ely and King’s Lynn once speed restrictions caused by ground conditions are lifted.

stories.brief: Proposals have been put forward to extend existing contracts for supported housing services. The plans, reported by the BBC, are currently under consideration. No further details regarding the duration of the extensions or the specific locations affected have been released at this time.

stories.brief: People living in an East Cambridgeshire village have raised concerns regarding a significant water leak in their local area. The issue was reported by residents who are worried about the scale of the water loss. Further details regarding the exact location of the leak or any potential impact on local services have not yet been provided.

stories.headline: New leadership appointments at sister schools
stories.brief: Two new headteachers have been appointed to lead a pair of sister schools. The move marks the beginning of a new chapter for the institutions. Further details regarding the specific schools involved or the names of the new appointees have not been released at this time.

stories.headline: Police update on investigation into baby's death
stories.brief: Cambridgeshire Police have provided a further update regarding two people arrested following the death of a three-month-old baby. The individuals were detained as part of an ongoing investigation into the circumstances surrounding the infant's passing. Authorities have not released further details at this stage as enquiries continue.

stories.headline: Hundreds protest against potential service cuts at Queen Elizabeth Hospital
stories.brief:
Hundreds of people gathered in King’s Lynn’s Tuesday Market Place last Saturday to protest against leaked proposals to downgrade A&E, maternity, and intensive care services at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital. North West Norfolk MP James Wild attended the demonstration, describing it as a powerful show of community support. 

Mr Wild has raised concerns in the House of Commons regarding the hospital's performance and the lack of transparency surrounding the potential service changes. He argued that removing local access to care would disadvantage residents in rural and coastal areas. The MP has called on the Health Secretary to reject any plans to reduce services, insisting that NHS bosses must prioritise the needs of local patients and maintain accessible care.

stories.headline: Woman sentenced for attempted arson in Cambridgeshire
stories.brief: Cambridgeshire Constabulary has reported that a woman has been convicted following an attempted arson attack on a neighbour. Police confirmed the incident involved a deliberate attempt to start a fire at a residential property. The woman has now been sentenced for her actions. No further details regarding the location or the specific date of the offence have been released by the authorities at this time.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn man fined for driving without a licence
stories.brief:
A 22-year-old man from North Lynn has been banned from driving for six months after being caught behind the wheel without a licence or insurance. Gentjan Capani, of Loke Road, was stopped by police on Tennyson Road on September 30. Officers had initially pulled the vehicle over due to suspicions regarding drugs, though no further details on that matter were provided.

Appearing at Lynn Magistrates’ Court on Thursday, Capani admitted to the offences. He told the court he is an asylum seeker without the right to work in the UK. In addition to the driving ban, he was ordered to pay a £120 fine, a £48 victim surcharge, and £50 in court costs.

stories.brief: Plans have been put forward to extend existing contracts for supported housing services. stories.brief: An MP is calling for an official investigation following an error regarding the approval of a school crossing scheme in March. stories.brief: Lincolnshire County Council has announced that essential roof replacement work is scheduled for Long Sutton Library. stories.brief: A resident of Orchard House Care Home in Wisbech has enjoyed a special return to his former football club. John Petch, who served as president of Wisbech Town Football Club for 16 years before stepping down in 2020, expressed a wish to see his hometown team play once more. Staff from the care home arranged for Mr Petch and his wife, Sheila, to attend Saturday’s match, which included lunch at Bygones.
